newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - February 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - February 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Chinese leaders Jiang Zemin and Li Peng cut short visits to return to Beijing on the reported deterioration of Deng Xiaoping's health.
-- More than seven people are arrested for vote-buying allegations during farmers' union election campaign.
-- Deng Xiaoping reportedly dying, Jiang Zemin and Li Peng cut short visits abroad.
-- Renowned Taiwan scholar Wu Chien-hsiung dies in New York at age of 85.
-- President Lee Teng-hui says he agrees issue of Vice-President Lien Chan concurrently serving as premier should be decided by ruling of Council of Grand Justices.
-- Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong hopes stock market can grow steadily, but central bank will keep close watch on recent sharp rises.
-- Deng Xiaoping's health reportedly deteriorating; Jiang Zemin and Li Peng return to Beijing.
-- Central bank concerned about huge turnover worth over T$100 billion in stock market.
-- Deng Xiaoping's health said to be deteriorating. -Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
